We replace $m$ with $4$ and $n$ with $6$ in the expression and simplify as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{n-2}{m-1}+\frac{2(m+1)}{n} & = \\ \frac{6-2}{4-1}+\frac{2(4+1)}{6} & = \\ \frac{4}{3}+\frac{2(5)}{6} & = \\ \frac{4}{3}+\frac{10}{6} & = \\ \frac{4}{3}+\frac{5}{3} & = \\ \frac{4+5}{3} & = \\ \frac{9}{3} & = \\ 3 & \end{aligned}
$$
